chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the women from being celibate and from withholding themselves from husbands.

key_terms.يَتَبَتَّلْنَ: to be celibate or remain unmarried

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid women regarding celibacy and marriage?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith records the Prophet’s prohibition against women practicing *tabattul* (celibacy or remaining unmarried) to emphasize the social and spiritual value of marriage. Shia scholars interpret this not as a mandatory obligation for all, but as a strong recommendation (*istihbab*) to preserve lineage and societal stability, contrasting with the Christian monastic tradition. It underscores the Islamic view of marriage as a natural state rather than a sacrifice to be renounced.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade the women that they be celibates and delay themselves from the marriage’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited women from ignoring themselves due to laziness and turning themselves of no benefit for their husbands.’”
